intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 7 units · geology to population · drawn for a phone
This book is not “world geography” — it is **Eritrea**. Outcomes: read the land’s story (rocks), water, climate, plants and animals, soils, how people make a living, and who lives where.

cards.title: 4.1 Introduction to Vegetation and Wildlife
body: Natural vegetation and wildlife are the direct reflection of climate and relief.
Eritrea has a varied relief and climate.
When climate changes, the type of vegetation also changes.
Eritrea is a tropical country with physical diversity characterized by highlands and lowlands.
For example, along the coastlines and continental shelves, there are mangrove forests, sea grass and sea weeds.

cards.title: 4.2 Vegetation Cover in Eritrea
body: At the beginning of this century, the forest cover was estimated to be 30% of the total landmass of Eritrea.
According to a recent estimate by the Ministry of Agriculture, the forest cover has been reduced to about 0.4%.
Due to the great variation in altitude, climate, and topography, the vegetation cover of Eritrea shows great differences in terms of species diversity and cover.
In the past, the Highlands of Eritrea were covered by upland evergreen forest such as juniper and olive trees and montane evergreen forests.
Montane evergreen forests are forests that grow in the Highlands.

cards.title: 4.3 Distribution of Natural Vegetation
body: Temperature decreases towards the Highlands while there is increase of rainfall.
The vegetation of the coastal plains of Eritrea is heterogeneous (diverse) in terms of both species diversity and distribution.
The vegetation here includes swamps along seasonal rivers and wadis, acacia woodland, semi desert acacia woodland, bush lands, desert scrubs and mangrove.
The shrubs are mainly 1 to 4 meters tall with scarce ground vegetation.
Mangroves are found along the coastal areas between the sea and the land.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which slow-growing highland forest tree species is native to the Eritrean high plateau?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify native highland conifers**
The native highland climax forests of Eritrea are composed of slow-growing conifers, specifically **Juniper (*Juniperus procera*)** and Wild Olive.

**Step 2: Compare other options**
* Eucalyptus: non-native/exotic.
* Doum Palm: riverine lowland.
* Mangrove: coastal intertidal.

**Step 3: Conclude**
The correct answer is Juniper.

cards.title: 4.4.1 Importance of forests
body: Forests also have recreational and aesthetic values.
The natural beauty and peace in forests offer a special source of enjoyment.
Many people throughout the world, use forests for different activities such as camping, hiking and hunting.
Many people also visit forests simply to enjoy themselvesand relax in the quiet beauty of forests.

cards.title: 4.4.2 The Importance of Tree Planting as a Source of Development
body: If natural vegetation is wisely managed, it provides a continuous source of wood and many other wood products.
The trees add nutrients to the soil through nitrogen fixation.

cards.title: 4.5 Environmental Issues
body: The largest part of Eritrea, particularly the central highlands where there is dense population, have been deforested.
Overgrazing and rapid urbanization also led to deforestation to a considerable degree.
Wild animals have lost their habitat and fled to neighboring states or died.
To do so, contact community leaders parents, or resource people from the Ministry of Agriculture.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Through photosynthesis, forest trees act as major carbon sinks by absorbing which atmospheric gas?
cards.why:
**Step 1: State the inputs of photosynthesis**
Trees absorb **Carbon dioxide ($$\text{CO}_2$$)** and water, utilizing solar energy to produce glucose and release Oxygen ($$\text{O}_2$$).

**Step 2: Conclude**
The absorbed gas is Carbon dioxide.

cards.title: Wildlife in Eritrea
body: **Wildlife (book examples):** African wild ass (arid north & Red Sea regions — globally endangered, relatively better off in Eritrea), Nubian ibex, elephant remnants in Gash-Barka (Haikota, Augaro, Antore), greater kudu, gazelles, warthog, ostrich, plus marine life (dugong, turtle). Threats: habitat loss, hunting, drought. Response: protected areas and conservation programmes.

cards.title: Exam sticky notes
body: - Wild ass = globally endangered, better in ER

cards.title: 4.6.1 Introduction
body: In the equatorial climate, rainfall is daily and heavy, while temperature and relative humidity are high.
In the savanna grassland, rainfall is seasonal.
The region is dominated by abundant animals.

cards.title: 4.6.2 Present Situation of Wildlife in Eritrea
body: Eritrea exhibits a wide variety of natural ecosystems that are well-distributed across the country.

Historically, Eritrea had a wide range of animal species such as elephant, hippopotamus, buffalo, giraffe, greater kudu, wild ass, Nubian ibex, water buck, lion, leopard, cheetah, colobus monkey, and others.
At present, some of these species exist in parts of Eritrea, but their number is small and is under threat.

In general, the number of wild animal in Eritrea has decreased considerably due to hunting, war, deforestation of the animal habitat, drought, the growth of towns and villages and the development of roads.

Natural vegetation and wildlife are the direct reflection of climate and relief.
Eritrea is a tropical country with physical diversity characterized by highlands and lowlands.

tips.text: Its climate is influenced by its latitudinal position, but physical diversity is the most important factor that determines the climate of Eritrea.
The climate varies from desert in the eastern Lowlands to temperate climate in the Highlands.
The natural vegetation and wildlife of Eritrea is the direct reflection of the climate.
In general, there is relationship among climate, natural vegetation, and wildlife in Eritrea.
Because of human activities such as cutting trees for agricultural purpose, timber, and fuel, vegetation cover has been reduced greatly.
Around 100 years ago, about 30% of Eritrea’s total area was covered by forests, but this has been reduced to 0.41% at present.
The present types of forests are Highland vegetation, acacia woodland, and riverine forests. There are also grasslands in the Lowlands.

The natural vegetation in Eritrea are classified into natural vegetation of eastern Lowlands, natural vegetation of eastern Escarpment, temperate vegetation of the Highlands, natural vegetation of western Escarpment, and vegetation of western Lowlands.
There are different kinds of wild animals in Eritrea. However their number has been reduced greatly due to deforestation and prolonged war.
The distribution of these wild animals is also influenced by topography.
Exam sticky notes: - Wild ass = globally endangered, better in ER

questions.q: The reasons why Eritrea shows a wide variety of wildlife are:
why: The textbook: Eritrea has a varied relief and climate, therefore it has varied natural vegetation and wildlife.
It also notes that the different vegetation types (acacia grassland, mountain vegetation, halophytic desert vegetation, mangroves) 'attract different kinds of animals'.
Altitude (relief), climate and vegetation all contribute. Answer: E.

similar.q: In Eritrea, the wildlife that is commonly found in Southern Red Sea region is  A) elephant.  B) wild ass.  C) lion.  D) ostrich.  E) B and D.
similar.a: E. B and D. — Elephants are in Gash-Barka and lions are no longer found there. So both B and D are correct. Answer: E.

questions.q: The type of natural vegetation found in the upper part of the Eastern Escarpment is:
why: The textbook: from the coast to the foot of the escarpment there are short umbrella-shaped acacias; 'Along the eastern Escarpment, there are olive trees and Juniper'; on the plateau, euphorbia and junipers.
Mangroves grow on the coast and islands; succulents and xerophytes in dry lowlands; savannah in the western lowlands.

questions.q: In Eritrea, the wild ass is mainly found in the
why: The textbook: 'This wild ass is found in Northern Red Sea region, Southern Red Sea region around the Ghel-alo and Thio localities, and the Anseba Region around Kerkebet.' The Southern Red Sea zone list also includes 'wild ass, ostrich'.
Its main stronghold is the arid south-eastern lowlands (Denkalia: Ghel-alo, Thio). Answer: A.
